source_text: Petrus namque apostolus ait: Christus pro nobis mortuus est, vobis relinquens exemplum, ut sequamini vestigia eius; qui peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore eius [n122] . Certe Apostoli sententia cum Dominica voce concordat. Dicit ille in Evangelio: Venit princeps mundi huius, et in me nihil invenit [n123] . Hoc idem commendat magister Ecclesiae, dicitque in Christo nullum fuisse delictum; sed per quid non habuerit peccatum veraci attestatione commendat. Quia, inquit, peccatum non fecit. Non dixit: Quia peccatum non suscepit, sed: Quia peccatum non fecit.
pass_a_gloss: For Peter the apostle says: Christ died for us, leaving you an example, that you may follow his footsteps; who did not do sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth. Certainly the Apostle's sentence agrees with the Lord's voice. He says in the Gospel: The prince of this world is coming, and he finds nothing in me. The teacher of the Church commends this same thing, and says there was no offense in Christ; but through what he did not have sin he commends by truthful attestation. Because, he says, he did not do sin. He did not say: Because he did not take up sin, but: Because he did not do sin.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: For the apostle Peter says: “Christ died for us, leaving you an example, so that you might follow his footsteps. He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth” (1 Peter 2:21–22). The apostle’s statement certainly agrees with the Lord’s voice. The Lord says in the Gospel, “The ruler of this world is coming, and he finds nothing in me” (John 14:30). The teacher of the Church commends the same point, saying there was no offense in Christ. But by truthful testimony he explains why Christ had no sin: “Because,” he says, “he committed no sin.” He did not say, “Because he received no sin,” but, “Because he committed no sin.”
